nodes.description: OER performance in AEM seawater electrolyzer (initial test)
nodes.source_text: Choi and co-workers assembled an AEM seawater electrolyzer with X37-50 Grade T (Dioxide Materials) as the membrane, Ni–FeOOH electrocatalyst as the anode... nodes.name: Pt@mh-3D MXene
nodes.source_text: Our group evaluated the stability of Pt@mh-3D MXene electrocatalysts in real seawater (Bohai Sea, China) for up to 250 h. The assembled system required an overpotential of 280 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA cm−2.

nodes.description: OER performance in AEM electrolyzer with alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: The AEM electrolyzer electrocatalyzed by NiFeCo-LDH exhibited a large current density (0.84 A cm−2) at a voltage of 1.7 V in alkaline seawater electrolyte. It could operate stably for 50 h at 0.5 A cm−2, and its FE reached 94%.

Tong and co-workers conducted HER tests in natural seawater using the Ni5P4 electrocatalyst. A low overpotential of 144 mV was required to achieve 10 mA cm−2, and the durability could be sustained for 40 h at 100 mA cm−2.

nodes.characterization_summary: MoO3-modified CoO array catalyst operated stably for 500 h at 1000 mA cm^-2 current density in real seawater two-electrode system.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the catalyst could be sustained for 500 h at an ampere-level current density of 1000 mA cm^-2 for the assembled two-electrode system in real seawater.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe/NiSx on nickel foam achieved 400 mA cm^-2 at 1.72 V cell voltage with >1000 h stability in 6 M KOH + 1.5 M NaCl at 80°C; no Cl2 detected, O2 yield and FE ~100%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared catalyst could achieve a current density of 400 mA cm^-2 and run stably for more than 1000 h in 6 M KOH + 1.5 M NaCl under industrial conditions at 80°C only by applying a cell voltage of 1.72 V in a single cell. The Cl2 was not detected, and the O2 yield and faradaic efficiency (FE) were both about 100%

nodes.characterization_summary: MnOx coating increased IrOx OER selectivity from 14% to >90% at 1.55 V vs RHE in Cl^--containing solution (pH ~0.9).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH required 359 mV overpotential at pH=13 (0.1 M KOH) vs 490 mV at pH=9.2 (0.3 M borate) to reach 10 mA cm^-2 in 0.5 M NaCl simulated seawater.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At pH = 13, an overpotential of only 359 mV was required to reach 10 mA cm^-2. At pH = 9.2, a high overpotential of about 490 mV was required to reach 10 mA cm^-2.
